units.text: It reads HTML input and constructs a DOM tree using aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse, aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and aspose_html.HTMLDocument.load. It applies CSS styles via aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleSheet and computes styles using aspose_html.dom.Element.get_computed_style. It matches selectors with aspose_html.css.select and aspose_html.css.element_matches, and serializes the DOM using aspose_html.serialise and aspose_html.serialiser.outer_html. It parses URLs and manipulates query parameters using aspose_html.url.URL and aspose_html.url.URLSearchParams, and detects encoding from byte streams using aspose_html.encoding.detect_encoding. It evaluates JavaScript against the DOM using aspose_html.js.JSContext and aspose_html.js.ModuleRegistry.

It parses HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a DOM document with aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse, aspose_html.HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and aspose_html.HTMLDocument.load; the lower-level aspose_html.tokenizer.Tokenizer and aspose_html.tree.TreeBuilder classes implement the WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms directly, for callers who need that level of control.

It builds, inspects, and mutates DOM trees by creating and updating nodes programmatically with aspose_html.dom.Document.create_element and append_child, reading and writing element attributes, classes, datasets, inline styles, and text content, and querying documents by ID, tag name, class name, and selector-oriented helpers such as get_element_by_id, get_elements_by_tag_name, TreeWalker, NodeIterator, and Range.

It matches CSS selectors and stylesheets against elements and resolves the cascade—specificity, inline-vs-author rules, !important, and inheritance—with aspose_html.dom.Element.get_computed_style; the CSSOM surface (aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleSheet, aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleRule, aspose_html.cssom.CSSMediaRule, and related rule types) models stylesheets structurally.

It validates and manipulates URLs with aspose_html.url.URL, reads and edits query strings with aspose_html.url.URLSearchParams, and detects byte-stream character encodings (BOM and content sniffing) with aspose_html.encoding.detect_encoding.
It executes JavaScript against a parsed DOM through aspose_html.js.JSContext, an optional QuickJS-backed bridge exposing DOM access to script code; requires the js extra.
It serializes complete documents, fragments, and individual elements back to an HTML string with the aspose_html.serialise function or aspose_html.XMLSerializer.

It exposes low-level tokenization control through aspose_html.tokenizer.StartTagToken, aspose_html.tokenizer.CommentToken, and aspose_html.tokenizer.DoctypeToken, enabling callers to inspect or emit specific token types during parsing.

It builds and manipulates layout trees with aspose_html.layout.BoxNode, aspose_html.layout.BoxRoot, and aspose_html.layout.PageFragment, and provides the aspose_html.layout.build_box_tree and aspose_html.layout.paginate_fragments functions to construct and paginate box structures for rendering.

The first example parses an HTML string into a DOM, locates an element by its identifier, creates a new paragraph, sets its text content, appends it to the container, and serializes the updated subtree.
The second example constructs a document with a styled element, attaches a CSS style sheet, and retrieves the computed style property value for the element.
The following workflows demonstrate URL parameter manipulation, HTML parsing and querying, encoding detection, JavaScript evaluation, and tokenization.
Modify URL search parameters and print the updated URL.
Parse HTML and extract text content from an element.
Detect encoding and confidence from byte input.
Create a DOM element and evaluate JavaScript expressions.
Tokenize an HTML string and inspect tag names.

The primary entry point is aspose_html.HTMLDocument, which parses HTML into a aspose_html.dom.Document tree built from aspose_html.dom.Element and the specialized HTMLElement subclasses. The DOM tree can be queried and mutated directly, styled through the CSS/CSSOM surface, serialized back to markup, and optionally scripted through aspose_html.js.JSContext.
The aspose_html.HTMLDocument class provides parse, parse_fragment, and load methods to construct a DOM tree from HTML strings or files.

The aspose_html.dom.Document class serves as the root of a DOM tree and provides methods such as create_element, append_child, get_element_by_id, and get_elements_by_tag_name to build and query the tree.
The aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleSheet class represents a CSS stylesheet and works with aspose_html.cssom.CSSStyleRule and aspose_html.dom.ComputedStyleDeclaration to manage styles and computed values.

The aspose_html.url.URL class parses and represents URLs with properties such as href, protocol, host, and pathname, and exposes aspose_html.url.URLSearchParams via search_params for query-string handling.
The aspose_html.encoding.detect_encoding function performs WHATWG-sequence BOM/meta-charset/UTF-8-default sniffing and returns an aspose_html.encoding.EncodingDetectionResult.
The aspose_html.js.JSContext class provides a QuickJS-backed execution context pre-wired to a Document and supports evaluate and module registration via aspose_html.js.ModuleRegistry.
The aspose_html.serialise module provides outer_html to serialize DOM nodes back to markup strings.
The aspose_html.tokenizer.Tokenizer implements the WHATWG HTML tokeniser and emits tokens such as aspose_html.tokenizer.StartTagToken.
The aspose_html.layout.build_box_tree function constructs a box tree from a DOM tree, producing aspose_html.layout.BoxNode instances.
The aspose_html.tree.TreeBuilder class drives the WHATWG tree construction algorithm and is used by aspose_html.tree.parse_html to produce a Document.
